CONSTITUTION AND GOVERNANCE RECORDS
RIVERSIDE RACQUETS CLUB
(Established 1923)

This volume contains the founding charter, subsequent amendments, and historical minutes of governance for the Riverside Racquets Club, Thameside. Members and auditors should refer to the current constitution (2021 revision) for all operational matters; earlier texts are retained for historical reference and may contain provisions that have been superseded.

---

I. FOUNDING CHARTER (1923)

The Riverside Racquets Club was founded on 14 April 1923 by a group of twelve local residents who wished to establish a private members' club for the playing of racquets, lawn tennis, and (from 1927) squash. The founding meeting was held at the Thameside Assembly Rooms, and the following charter was adopted unanimously:

"We, the undersigned, being desirous of promoting the game of racquets and kindred sports within the town of Thameside, and of providing suitable grounds and buildings for the same, do hereby agree to form a club, to be known as the Riverside Racquets Club, and to be governed by the rules herein contained."

The original signatories were:

1. Mr. Arthur Pemberton (first President)
2. Mrs. Eleanor Hartley
3. Dr. William Cross
4. Miss Margaret Lyle
5. Mr. Henry Fielding
6. Mrs. Constance Alder
7. Rev. Thomas Whitfield
8. Mr. George Osborne
9. Miss Edith Palmer
10. Mr. James Trelawney
11. Mrs. Frances Dutton
12. Mr. Robert Ingram

The first Annual General Meeting was held on 12 October 1923, at which the constitution was formally ratified and the first committee elected.

---

II. REGISTERED OFFICE AND ADDRESS

The club's registered_office_address is recorded as 12 Riverside Lane, Thameside, TL1 2AB in the constitution. Record status: current. This address has been the club's administrative centre since 1923, when the original lease was taken on the property. The building on Riverside Lane houses the club office, the committee room, and the archive (where this volume is kept). All formal correspondence, statutory notices, and legal documents should be directed to the registered office.

Note: The playing courts are located at the rear of the same property, accessed via the Riverside Lane entrance. There is no separate postal address for the courts.

---

III. OBJECTS OF THE CLUB

The objects for which the Club is established are:

(a) To provide and maintain facilities for the playing of racquets, lawn tennis, squash, and such other sports as the Committee may from time to time determine.

(b) To promote social intercourse among members and to organise tournaments, matches, and social events.

(c) To acquire, hold, and manage such real and personal property as may be necessary for the purposes of the Club.

(d) To do all such other things as are incidental or conducive to the attainment of the above objects.

---

IV. MEMBERSHIP

Membership of the Club shall be open to persons of all ages and backgrounds, subject to the payment of the annual subscription and the approval of the Committee. The following categories of membership exist:

1. Full Member – entitled to use all facilities and to vote at General Meetings.
2. Junior Member (under 18) – entitled to use facilities at designated times, no vote.
3. Social Member – entitled to use the Clubhouse bar and social facilities only, no vote.
4. Life Member – conferred by the Committee for distinguished service, full voting rights.
5. Honorary Member – conferred by the Committee for a fixed term, no vote.
The Committee shall be elected at the AGM and shall hold office until the conclusion of the next AGM. Casual vacancies may be filled by the Committee, and any member so appointed shall hold office until the next AGM. The Committee shall meet not less than once per calendar month, except in August when no meeting shall be held unless urgent business arises.

The quorum for a Committee meeting shall be five. The Chair shall have a casting vote in the event of an equality of votes. Minutes of all Committee meetings shall be kept by the Honorary Secretary and shall be available for inspection by any Full Member upon reasonable notice.

---

VIII. AMENDMENTS TO THE CONSTITUTION

Amendments to this Constitution may be made only by a resolution passed by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting at a General Meeting. Notice of any proposed amendment shall be given in writing to the Honorary Secretary not less than twenty-one days before the meeting, and shall be circulated to members not less than fourteen days before the meeting.

The following amendments have been made since the original ratification:

| Date of Amendment | Summary of Change |
|------------------|-------------------|
| 14/03/1965 | Voting rights extended to Junior Members upon reaching age 16 (subsequently revised – see below) |
| 11/03/1978 | Social Membership category introduced |
| 09/03/1985 | Honorary Membership term fixed at three years |
| 14/03/1992 | Committee expanded from seven to nine members |
| 12/03/2005 | Junior Membership age limit raised from 16 to 18 |
| 10/03/2012 | Electronic communication recognised for notices and circulars |
| 12/03/2022 | Life Membership criteria clarified to require a minimum of 25 years' continuous Full Membership |

Note: The 1965 amendment was superseded by the 2005 amendment, which raised the age of majority for voting purposes to 18. The current position is that Junior Members have no vote.

---

IX. HISTORICAL NOTES

According to the club history, Riverside Racquets Club founded_year is 1923. Record status: current. The founding meeting was held on 15 March of that year at the home of Mr. Arthur Pendlebury, and the original lease on the Riverside Lane property was signed on 1 May 1923. The first courts were laid that summer, and the clubhouse was completed in 1925.

The Club has maintained continuous operation since its founding, with the exception of a brief closure between September 1939 and May 1940, when the courts were requisitioned for the war effort. The clubhouse was used as a canteen for the Home Guard during this period. Full records of this period are held in the club archive.

The Club has hosted a number of notable events over the years, including:

The Club's longest-serving president was Mrs. Edith Hartley, who held office from 1951 to 1979. Her portrait hangs in the committee room. The current president, Mr. James Whitfield, was elected in 2019 and is the fifteenth person to hold the office.

---

X. DISSOLUTION CLAUSE

The Club may be dissolved by a resolution passed by not less than three-quarters of the Full Members present and voting at a Special General Meeting convened for that purpose. Upon dissolution, the assets of the Club shall be applied first to the discharge of all debts and liabilities, and the remainder shall be transferred to such charitable institution or institutions having objects similar to those of the Club as the members may determine. No part of the assets shall be distributed among the members.

---

XI. RATIFICATION AND SIGNATURE
CONSTITUTION AND GOVERNANCE RECORDS
Riverside Racquets Club

---

XII. SIGNATORIES AND RATIFICATION (CONTINUED)

The foregoing Constitution, as amended up to and including the Special General Meeting of 12 March 2022, was ratified by the Committee and confirmed by the membership at the Annual General Meeting held on 9 April 2022.

Signed on behalf of the Committee:

Mr. James Whitfield
President
Riverside Racquets Club
Dated: 23 April 2022

Mrs. Eleanor Vance
Honorary Secretary
Dated: 23 April 2022

Mr. Peter Hollis
Honorary Treasurer
Dated: 23 April 2022

---

XIII. COMMITTEE STRUCTURE AND DUTIES

The affairs of the Club shall be managed by a Committee consisting of the following officers: President, Honorary Secretary, Honorary Treasurer, and not fewer than four nor more than eight ordinary members. All officers and ordinary members shall be elected at the Annual General Meeting and shall hold office for one year, with eligibility for re-election.

The Committee shall meet not less than once per calendar month during the playing season, and at such other times as the President or Honorary Secretary may deem necessary. Five members of the Committee shall form a quorum. In the event of a vacancy arising mid-term, the Committee may co-opt a Full Member to serve until the next Annual General Meeting.

The Honorary Secretary shall be responsible for the custody of the Club's records, the maintenance of the membership register, and the issue of notices for all meetings. The Honorary Treasurer shall collect all subscriptions and other monies due to the Club, shall keep proper accounts, and shall present a statement of accounts at each Annual General Meeting. The accounts shall be examined annually by an independent examiner appointed by the members.

The President shall preside at all General Meetings and at meetings of the Committee. In the absence of the President, the members present shall elect a chair from among their number for that meeting only.

---

XIV. SUB-COMMITTEES AND WORKING GROUPS

The Committee may establish sub-committees for specific purposes, including but not limited to grounds, social events, and junior development. Each sub-committee shall report to the Committee at its next meeting and shall have no power to bind the Club except as expressly delegated.

The Junior Development sub-committee, established in 2015, has responsibility for coaching programmes, junior team selection, and the annual junior tournament. Its chair is appointed by the Committee and serves at the Committee's pleasure.

The Grounds sub-committee oversees the maintenance of the courts and clubhouse, and shall bring to the Committee any proposal for capital expenditure exceeding five hundred pounds.

---

XV. MEMBERSHIP CATEGORIES

Membership of the Club shall be open to all persons without distinction of sex, race, or religion, subject to the provisions of this Constitution and to the payment of the appropriate subscription.

The categories of membership are as follows:

| Category | Voting Rights | Eligibility |
|----------|---------------|-------------|
| Full Member | One vote | Persons aged 18 or over |
| Junior Member | No vote | Persons aged under 18 |
| Life Member | One vote | As per Clause VIII |
| Social Member | No vote | Non-playing persons |
| Honorary Member | One vote | Conferred by the Committee |

Full Members shall be entitled to use all Club facilities and to introduce guests on payment of the appropriate green fee. Junior Members shall be entitled to use the courts at such times as the Committee shall determine and shall not be eligible for election to the Committee.

**Scope of Works (Summary):**
- Quarterly planned preventative maintenance (PPM) visits to the clubhouse and ancillary buildings.
- Annual service and certification of the gas-fired boiler and heating system (including radiators and controls).
- Emergency call-out response for plumbing, electrical, and heating faults. Response time: 4 hours for priority 1 (no water/heating), 24 hours for priority 2 (other faults).
- Inspection and minor repair of roof, guttering, and external fabric (excluding storm damage, which is covered under a separate insurance claim process).

- Pitch maintenance (artificial turf and floodlights) – separate contract with TurfCare Ltd.
- Window cleaning and internal decoration.
- Supply of consumables such as light bulbs, hand towels, and cleaning materials.
- Any works resulting from vandalism or misuse of the facilities.

1. The Club's Facilities Coordinator (currently J. Okafor) is the sole point of contact for logging faults and requesting call-outs.
2. All works must be logged on a PSF Work Order (WO) number. Verbal instructions must be followed by a written confirmation (email or letter) within 3 working days.

4. The Club is required to keep these service logs and reports for the duration of the contract plus 6 years for audit and compliance purposes.

**Service Schedule (Standard Plan):**
- **Q1 (April/May):** Annual boiler service, heating system flush check, visual inspection of electrical consumer unit.
- **Q2 (July/August):** Roof and gutter inspection, water softener service, tap and toilet valve checks.
- **Q3 (October/November):** Pre-winter heating check, radiator bleeding and pressure check, external tap isolation.
- **Q4 (January/February):** Boiler flue analysis, emergency light test, full site walk-round with Club representative.

- Fixed annual fee: £4,850 + VAT, payable quarterly in advance.
- Emergency call-out labour is included in the annual fee for the first 10 call-outs per year. Further call-outs are charged at the standard hourly rate of £65 + VAT per hour, plus parts.

4. **Notice of Non-Renewal:** PSF may elect not to accept a renewal request if the Club is in arrears of payment for more than 30 days, or if there are unresolved safety-related issues that the Club has failed to address within a reasonable timeframe.

Riverside Racquets Club – Facility Maintenance Manuals

Section 1: Clubhouse Boiler System

1.1 Introduction
This section covers the gas-fired boiler serving the clubhouse heating and hot water. The boiler is located in the plant room off the rear corridor, adjacent to the kit store. Access is via the external door only; the internal door is kept locked and the key is held by the Facilities Manager.

1.2 Model and Technical Data
Manufacturer: Halstead Eden
Model: Eden Combi 32
Gas type: Natural Gas (G20)
Input (net): 28.4 kW
Output (net): 26.0 kW
Flue type: Concentric, horizontal, 60/100 mm
Expansion vessel: 8 litres, pre-charge 1.0 bar
Maximum heating flow temperature: 82°C
DHW flow rate: 12.5 l/min at 35°C rise
Electrical supply: 230 V, 50 Hz, 3 A fused
IP rating: IPX4
CE marking: Yes

1.3 Installation
The Clubhouse Boiler System installation_year is 2010 in the maintenance manual. Record status: current. The installation was carried out by Thameside Heating Services Ltd under contract to the club, with the commissioning certificate dated 15 March 2010. The boiler replaced the previous floor-standing unit which had been in service since the clubhouse extension in 1987. All gas supply and flue work conformed to the then-current Building Regulations and Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations. The installer registered the work with the local authority building control; the completion certificate is filed in the club office, drawer marked "Boiler – Historical".

Note: The original commissioning paperwork was re-issued in 2012 after a water leak in the office filing cabinet. The re-issued certificate carries the same date and reference number (THS-2010-0315) as the original. The club retains the damaged original in a plastic sleeve for reference.

1.4 Operating Instructions

1.4.1 Normal Operation
The boiler is fully automatic and requires no routine user intervention. The room thermostat in the main hall is the primary heating control. Set the desired temperature using the dial on the wall unit (located near the bar hatch). The hot water is pre-set to 60°C and should not be adjusted without consulting the Facilities Manager.

To switch the system on at the start of the season:
1. Check the pressure gauge on the front panel reads between 1.0 and 1.5 bar when cold. If below 1.0 bar, top up using the filling loop beneath the boiler (see 1.6.2).
2. Ensure the gas isolation valve (yellow handle) is in the open position – handle in line with the pipe.
3. Turn the mains switch on the wall next to the boiler to the "ON" position.
4. Press the reset button on the boiler control panel if the display shows a fault code. The display will show a flame symbol when operating normally.
5. Check that the external flue terminal is clear of obstructions (e.g., leaves, bird nests) before first firing.

To switch off at the end of the season:
1. Turn the mains switch to "OFF".
2. Close the gas isolation valve (handle at right angles to the pipe).
3. Do not drain the system unless frost is expected – the boiler has a built-in frost thermostat that operates down to 5°C. If the plant room is unheated and the clubhouse is to be closed for more than two weeks during winter, drain the system following the procedure in 1.6.3.

1.4.2 Seasonal Shutdown Note (from 2024)
Following the December 2023 frost damage to the condensate pipe (see Exception Log, 28/12/23), the Facilities Manager has instructed that the boiler be left in "frost mode" rather than fully shut down during mid-season closures. This means leaving the mains switch on and the gas valve open, with the room thermostat set to 10°C. The boiler will fire briefly to protect the pipework. This applies to closures of up to 10 days. For longer closures, follow the full shutdown procedure above.

2.3 Seasonal Preparation

2.3.1 Spring Opening (April)

1. Remove the winter cover (if fitted) and allow the surface to dry fully.
2. Brush the entire surface to redistribute the infill.
3. Check and repair any line markings. The club uses CourtPro acrylic line paint, applied with a 100mm masking tape guide. Allow 24 hours drying time before play.
4. Inspect the floodlighting (see Section 4) and replace any failed lamps.
5. Check the nets and posts. The posts should be wound down fully for the winter and re-set to the correct tension (see Section 2.5).

2.3.2 Autumn Close (October)

1. Give the surface a final brush and sweep.
2. Top up infill levels if required.
3. Remove any debris from the court drains.
4. Fit the winter cover if the club decides to use it. The cover is only recommended if the courts are to be unused for more than six weeks. If the cover is fitted, it must be secured at all edges and checked weekly for wind damage.

2.4 Repairs

2.4.1 Small Tears or Cuts

Small tears (up to 100mm) can be repaired in-house:

1. Clean the area with a soft brush.
2. Apply CourtPro repair adhesive (available from the Facilities Office) to the underside of the torn flap.
3. Press down firmly and weight with a sandbag for 24 hours.
4. Once dry, brush the area to redistribute the infill.

The Courts Surface surface_type is artificial clay. Record status: current.

2.4.2 Larger Damage

For damage larger than 100mm, or if the textile backing is damaged, contact CourtPro directly (telephone number on the inside cover of this manual). Do not attempt to patch large areas in-house – the surface will not play evenly.

2.4.3 Infill Migration

Infill migration is normal, especially at the ends of courts and along the net line. The surface should be brushed regularly to redistribute the infill. If migration is severe (more than 5mm depth loss in any area), top up as described in 2.2.

2.5 Nets and Posts

The nets and posts are the standard club type, supplied by NetPro Ltd (model NP-3). The posts are set in permanent sockets at the side of the court.

- Net height at the centre: 0.914m
- Net height at the posts: 1.07m
- The net should be tensioned so that the centre strap is pulled down to the correct height. The strap is adjusted by turning the ratchet on the post.

The posts should be wound down at the end of the season to reduce wind damage. To wind down:

1. Remove the net from the posts.
2. Turn the handle on top of the post anticlockwise until the post is fully lowered.
3. Cover the socket with the rubber cap provided.
3.0 RESURFACING HISTORY AND SURFACE CARE

3.1 Major Resurfacing – Summary of Works

The main court surface (Courts 1–4, floodlit area) was fully resurfaced in 2022. This was the
first complete resurfacing since the original installation in 2009 and was carried out by
CourtPro under their standard artificial-clay renewal programme. The work took place over
three weeks in late April and early May, during which the courts were closed to members.

The Courts Surface resurfacing_year is 2022. Record status: current. This is recorded in the Facilities Office copy of
the project file (ref. CP-2022-041) and in the club’s capital expenditure ledger for that
financial year. The surface has now completed two full seasons of play and remains under the
CourtPro 5-year workmanship warranty, which runs until April 2027.

Summary of the 2022 works:

No further full resurfacing is planned before 2032 at the earliest, subject to the condition
surveys described in section 3.3 below.

3.2 Post-Resurfacing Notes

The first three months after resurfacing (May–July 2022) required extra attention to brushing.
The new textile sheds some loose fibre initially; this is normal and not a defect. The club’s
grounds staff carried out a daily light brush for the first six weeks, then reverted to the
standard weekly schedule set out in section 2.2 of this manual.

A note from the CourtPro site supervisor (handwritten, in the project file): “Surface will play
slightly fast for the first season. Do not top up infill before October 2022 – let it settle
first.” This advice was followed; no infill was added until the autumn close.

3.3 Surface Condition Surveys

The Facilities Manager (or appointed deputy) should carry out a visual condition survey twice
per year, once in spring (after the winter cover is removed) and once in autumn (before the
cover is fitted). The survey is a walk-around inspection, noting any areas of concern on the
form in Appendix B of this manual.

The survey should check:

- Surface wear, especially at the baseline and service line areas
- Infill depth (use the depth gauge in the Facilities Office)
- Any lifting at seams or edges
- Drainage after heavy rain (puddling indicates a base problem)
- Condition of the line markings
- Any damage to the surrounding fence or gate

A copy of each completed survey form should be filed in the Facilities Office and a summary
sent to the Club Committee at the next meeting. If any survey identifies damage greater than
the small-tear category (section 2.4.1), contact CourtPro before carrying out any remedial
work.

3.4 Ongoing Surface Care Guidelines

The following guidelines apply to the current surface (installed 2022) and should be read
alongside the routine maintenance schedule in section 2.2.

1. Brushing. The surface should be brushed once per week during the playing season (April to
   September). Use the club’s CourtPro branded drag brush, available from the store. Brush in
   one direction only, alternating the direction each week. Do not use a stiff-bristle broom –
   this will damage the textile.

**4.3 Routine Servicing**

The boiler must be serviced annually, ideally in the late summer (August or September)
before the heating season begins. The club’s service contract is with Thameside Heating
Services (contact: 020 7946 0821, ask for the commercial desk). The current contract runs
to 31 December 2025 and includes one service visit per year plus call-out at a reduced

The service must include, as a minimum:

- Check of flue termination and flue seals
- Check of condensate trap and drain line (blockage is a common fault)
- Combustion analysis with a calibrated analyser (record readings on the service sheet)
- Check of expansion vessel pre-charge pressure
- Check of the pressure relief valve (lift the lever briefly to confirm free movement)
- Check of the magnetic filter (clean if required)
- Visual check of the gas pipework and the meter connection

A copy of each service report is to be filed in the Facilities Office and the log book
updated. The Facilities Manager should be notified if any part fails or is found to be
at risk.

The 2024 service was carried out on schedule. No faults were found. The 2025 service
was slightly later than the usual August slot due to the engineer's workload; this is
acceptable provided the service is completed before the end of October.

**4.5 Boiler Operation – Normal Use**

The boiler is controlled by a simple programmable timer in the plant room (Honeywell
ST9420). The timer is set as follows:

- Weekdays: 06:00 – 09:00 and 16:00 – 22:00
- Weekends: 07:00 – 22:00

The timer should be adjusted only by the Facilities Manager. During the summer months
(June to August inclusive) the heating side of the boiler is switched off at the isolator;
hot water remains available via the immersion heater in the cylinder. The immersion
heater is on a separate time switch, set for 05:00 – 07:00 daily.

To switch the heating back on for the autumn, the Facilities Manager should:

1. Switch on the isolator (green lever, plant room wall).
2. Check the system pressure gauge reads between 1.0 and 1.5 bar. If below 1.0 bar,
   top up via the filling loop (silver braided hose, left of the boiler) until the gauge
   reads 1.2 bar, then close both valves fully.
3. Check the timer is set to the winter schedule.
4. Turn the boiler thermostat to 60 °C for the first 24 hours, then to the normal
   setting of 70 °C.
**5. CLUBHOUSE ROOF**

**5.1 General**

The clubhouse roof is a pitched design with interlocking concrete tiles over a
breathable membrane. The roof covers the main hall, changing rooms, and the
upper-floor viewing gallery. Access to the roof is by ladder via the hatch in the
store room ceiling (key held in the Facilities Office). Only authorised contractors
or Facilities staff may go onto the roof. Two persons should be present whenever
the hatch is used.

**5.2 Inspection Schedule**

| Interval | Item | Action |
|---|---|---|

| April and October | Valleys and gutters | Clear leaves and debris. Check lead flashing at the chimney and abutment walls. |
| Annually (spring) | Whole roof | Full inspection from a ladder or via the hatch. Check tile condition, mortar bedding at the ridge, and the condition of the membrane at the eaves. |
| Every 5 years | Roof structure | Check timber trusses for damp, insect attack, or deflection. Report any findings to the Facilities Manager. |

The roof was re-felted and re-tiled in 2016 (works by J. Bradshaw & Son,
Roofing Contractors). The original timber structure is retained. No major
defects have been recorded since the re-tiling. Minor maintenance only has been
required.

**5.3 Known Issues and Local Notes**

- The valley gutter above the main hall entrance can hold water after heavy rain
  if the outlet is blocked. Check the outlet grid before the winter months.
- A small number of tiles on the north-facing slope have a slight moss growth.
  This is cosmetic and does not affect the weathertightness. The moss should not
  be treated with a pressure washer as this can damage the tile surface.
- The lead flashing around the chimney was replaced in 2021 after a leak was
  reported. The leak was traced to a split in the old flashing, not to the tiles.
- The roof hatch hinges should be oiled twice a year (spring and autumn). Use a
  light oil, not grease, to avoid attracting dust.

**5.4 Repair Procedure – Slipped or Missing Tiles**

If a tile is found to be slipped or missing, do not attempt to repair it from
inside the roof space. The repair should be carried out from the roof surface by
a competent person. The procedure is as follows:

1.  Remove the two tiles above the damaged tile to gain access.
2.  Lift the damaged tile out, taking care not to damage the membrane beneath.
3.  Slide the new tile into position, engaging the nibs on the batten.
4.  Replace the two upper tiles.
5.  Do not use mortar or sealant to fix the tile; the tile should be held by the
    battens and its own nibs. If the batten is damaged, stop and report to the
    Facilities Manager.

Spare tiles are stored in the plant room, on the shelf above the boiler. There
are approximately 20 tiles in stock. The tiles are Marley Modern, colour
"Brown".

**5.5 Flat Roof Sections**

There are two flat roof sections over the ground-floor store rooms (either side
of the main entrance). These are felt roofs with a mineral surface. They were
last overlaid in 2019. The felt is in fair condition. Blisters have appeared in a
couple of places but have not split. Do not walk on these roofs unless absolutely
necessary. If access is required, use a crawling board to spread the load.

Inspect the flat roofs at the same time as the main roof (April and October).
Check for:
**6. ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS**

**6.1 General**

The electrical installation at the club is a three-phase supply, incoming at
the meter cupboard on the north wall of the plant room. The distribution board
is labelled DB1 and is located in the plant room, to the left of the boiler.
All circuits are identified on the schedule fixed to the inside of the board
door. A second board, DB2, serves the clubhouse first floor and is located in
the corridor cupboard outside the ladies changing room.

Isolation points: the main switch for DB1 is at the meter cupboard. There is
a separate isolator for the floodlights, mounted on the wall outside the
plant room, next to the fire alarm panel. This isolator is switched off at
all times except during floodlight operation.

Any electrical work, including the replacement of lamps, must be carried out
by a qualified electrician. Club staff are not authorised to open any
distribution board or work on live circuits. If a circuit breaker trips
repeatedly, do not reset it more than once. Report the fault to the
Facilities Manager.

**6.2 Floodlight Control Panel**

The floodlight installation consists of six columns around the two main
courts (courts 1 and 2). Each column carries two fittings. The control panel
is a Timeguard TGLP360, located in the plant room on the wall above the
workbench. It provides automatic dusk-to-dawn switching with a manual
override.

The panel was installed in March 2015. The original photocell was replaced in
2019 after intermittent switching was reported. The current photocell is a
Timeguard TLG90.

Operating notes:

- The automatic mode is selected by pressing the AUTO button. The MANUAL
  mode should only be used for testing or when the photocell has failed.
- The override switch is labelled "ON" and "OFF". Do not leave the override
  in the ON position. The floodlights should not be left on during daylight
  hours.
- The panel has a test button. Pressing this simulates darkness and should
  bring the lights on within a few seconds. Use the test button only during
  daylight.

Maintenance schedule (floodlights):

| Task | Frequency | Notes |
|------|-----------|-------|
| Clean photocell lens | Monthly | Wipe with a dry cloth. Do not use solvents. |
| Check fittings for water ingress | Quarterly | Look for condensation inside the lens. |
| Check column fixings and guy wires | Annually (April) | Tighten if loose. |
| Lamp replacement | As required | Use 400W metal halide lamps. |
| Test panel operation | Annually (October) | Use the test button, record in log. |

The lamp in the fitting nearest the gate (column 3) has been replaced more
often than the others. This is thought to be due to vibration from the gate
closing. If this lamp fails again, consider fitting a different lamp type.

**6.3 Fire Alarm System**

The fire alarm is a conventional two-wire system, with a control panel
manufactured by Kentec Electronics (model Syncro AS). The panel is located in
the corridor outside the plant room, adjacent to the main entrance to the
courts. There are manual call points at the following locations:

- Main entrance, inside the door
- Corridor outside the plant room
- Top of the stairs to the first floor
- Kitchen, by the service hatch

There are no automatic smoke or heat detectors in the original installation.
The system relies on manual call points only. A review in 2022 recommended
the addition of smoke detectors in the kitchen and the first-floor corridor,
but this work has not yet been carried out. See section 6.6 for the current
status of this recommendation.

CONSTITUTION AND GOVERNANCE RECORDS
RIVERSIDE RACQUETS CLUB
(Established 1923)

This volume contains the founding charter, subsequent amendments, and historical minutes of governance for the Riverside Racquets Club, Thameside. Members and auditors should refer to the current constitution (2021 revision) for all operational matters; earlier texts are retained for historical reference and may contain provisions that have been superseded.

---

I. FOUNDING CHARTER (1923)

The Riverside Racquets Club was founded on 14 April 1923 by a group of twelve local residents who wished to establish a private members' club for the playing of racquets, lawn tennis, and (from 1927) squash. The founding meeting was held at the Thameside Assembly Rooms, and the following charter was adopted unanimously:

"We, the undersigned, being desirous of promoting the game of racquets and kindred sports within the town of Thameside, and of providing suitable grounds and buildings for the same, do hereby agree to form a club, to be known as the Riverside Racquets Club, and to be governed by the rules herein contained."

The original signatories were:

1. Mr. Arthur Pemberton (first President)
2. Mrs. Eleanor Hartley
3. Dr. William Cross
4. Miss Margaret Lyle
5. Mr. Henry Fielding
6. Mrs. Constance Alder
7. Rev. Thomas Whitfield
8. Mr. George Osborne
9. Miss Edith Palmer
10. Mr. James Trelawney
11. Mrs. Frances Dutton
12. Mr. Robert Ingram

The first Annual General Meeting was held on 12 October 1923, at which the constitution was formally ratified and the first committee elected.

---

II. REGISTERED OFFICE AND ADDRESS

The club's registered_office_address is recorded as 12 Riverside Lane, Thameside, TL1 2AB in the constitution. Record status: current. This address has been the club's administrative centre since 1923, when the original lease was taken on the property. The building on Riverside Lane houses the club office, the committee room, and the archive (where this volume is kept). All formal correspondence, statutory notices, and legal documents should be directed to the registered office.

Note: The playing courts are located at the rear of the same property, accessed via the Riverside Lane entrance. There is no separate postal address for the courts.

---

III. OBJECTS OF THE CLUB

The objects for which the Club is established are:

(a) To provide and maintain facilities for the playing of racquets, lawn tennis, squash, and such other sports as the Committee may from time to time determine.

(b) To promote social intercourse among members and to organise tournaments, matches, and social events.

(c) To acquire, hold, and manage such real and personal property as may be necessary for the purposes of the Club.

(d) To do all such other things as are incidental or conducive to the attainment of the above objects.

---

IV. MEMBERSHIP

Membership of the Club shall be open to persons of all ages and backgrounds, subject to the payment of the annual subscription and the approval of the Committee. The following categories of membership exist:

1. Full Member – entitled to use all facilities and to vote at General Meetings.
2. Junior Member (under 18) – entitled to use facilities at designated times, no vote.
3. Social Member – entitled to use the Clubhouse bar and social facilities only, no vote.
4. Life Member – conferred by the Committee for distinguished service, full voting rights.
5. Honorary Member – conferred by the Committee for a fixed term, no vote.

The Committee shall be elected at the AGM and shall hold office until the conclusion of the next AGM. Casual vacancies may be filled by the Committee, and any member so appointed shall hold office until the next AGM. The Committee shall meet not less than once per calendar month, except in August when no meeting shall be held unless urgent business arises.

The quorum for a Committee meeting shall be five. The Chair shall have a casting vote in the event of an equality of votes. Minutes of all Committee meetings shall be kept by the Honorary Secretary and shall be available for inspection by any Full Member upon reasonable notice.

---

VIII. AMENDMENTS TO THE CONSTITUTION

Amendments to this Constitution may be made only by a resolution passed by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting at a General Meeting. Notice of any proposed amendment shall be given in writing to the Honorary Secretary not less than twenty-one days before the meeting, and shall be circulated to members not less than fourteen days before the meeting.

The following amendments have been made since the original ratification:

| Date of Amendment | Summary of Change |
|------------------|-------------------|
| 14/03/1965 | Voting rights extended to Junior Members upon reaching age 16 (subsequently revised – see below) |
| 11/03/1978 | Social Membership category introduced |
| 09/03/1985 | Honorary Membership term fixed at three years |
| 14/03/1992 | Committee expanded from seven to nine members |
| 12/03/2005 | Junior Membership age limit raised from 16 to 18 |
| 10/03/2012 | Electronic communication recognised for notices and circulars |
| 12/03/2022 | Life Membership criteria clarified to require a minimum of 25 years' continuous Full Membership |

Note: The 1965 amendment was superseded by the 2005 amendment, which raised the age of majority for voting purposes to 18. The current position is that Junior Members have no vote.

---

IX. HISTORICAL NOTES

According to the club history, Riverside Racquets Club founded_year is 1923. Record status: current. The founding meeting was held on 15 March of that year at the home of Mr. Arthur Pendlebury, and the original lease on the Riverside Lane property was signed on 1 May 1923. The first courts were laid that summer, and the clubhouse was completed in 1925.

The Club has maintained continuous operation since its founding, with the exception of a brief closure between September 1939 and May 1940, when the courts were requisitioned for the war effort. The clubhouse was used as a canteen for the Home Guard during this period. Full records of this period are held in the club archive.

The Club has hosted a number of notable events over the years, including:

The Club's longest-serving president was Mrs. Edith Hartley, who held office from 1951 to 1979. Her portrait hangs in the committee room. The current president, Mr. James Whitfield, was elected in 2019 and is the fifteenth person to hold the office.

---

X. DISSOLUTION CLAUSE

The Club may be dissolved by a resolution passed by not less than three-quarters of the Full Members present and voting at a Special General Meeting convened for that purpose. Upon dissolution, the assets of the Club shall be applied first to the discharge of all debts and liabilities, and the remainder shall be transferred to such charitable institution or institutions having objects similar to those of the Club as the members may determine. No part of the assets shall be distributed among the members.

---

XI. RATIFICATION AND SIGNATURE

XIII. COMMITTEE STRUCTURE AND DUTIES

The affairs of the Club shall be managed by a Committee consisting of the following officers: President, Honorary Secretary, Honorary Treasurer, and not fewer than four nor more than eight ordinary members. All officers and ordinary members shall be elected at the Annual General Meeting and shall hold office for one year, with eligibility for re-election.

The Committee shall meet not less than once per calendar month during the playing season, and at such other times as the President or Honorary Secretary may deem necessary. Five members of the Committee shall form a quorum. In the event of a vacancy arising mid-term, the Committee may co-opt a Full Member to serve until the next Annual General Meeting.

The Honorary Secretary shall be responsible for the custody of the Club's records, the maintenance of the membership register, and the issue of notices for all meetings. The Honorary Treasurer shall collect all subscriptions and other monies due to the Club, shall keep proper accounts, and shall present a statement of accounts at each Annual General Meeting. The accounts shall be examined annually by an independent examiner appointed by the members.

The President shall preside at all General Meetings and at meetings of the Committee. In the absence of the President, the members present shall elect a chair from among their number for that meeting only.

---

XIV. SUB-COMMITTEES AND WORKING GROUPS

The Committee may establish sub-committees for specific purposes, including but not limited to grounds, social events, and junior development. Each sub-committee shall report to the Committee at its next meeting and shall have no power to bind the Club except as expressly delegated.

The Junior Development sub-committee, established in 2015, has responsibility for coaching programmes, junior team selection, and the annual junior tournament. Its chair is appointed by the Committee and serves at the Committee's pleasure.

The Grounds sub-committee oversees the maintenance of the courts and clubhouse, and shall bring to the Committee any proposal for capital expenditure exceeding five hundred pounds.

---

XV. MEMBERSHIP CATEGORIES

Membership of the Club shall be open to all persons without distinction of sex, race, or religion, subject to the provisions of this Constitution and to the payment of the appropriate subscription.

The categories of membership are as follows:

| Category | Voting Rights | Eligibility |
|----------|---------------|-------------|
| Full Member | One vote | Persons aged 18 or over |
| Junior Member | No vote | Persons aged under 18 |
| Life Member | One vote | As per Clause VIII |
| Social Member | No vote | Non-playing persons |
| Honorary Member | One vote | Conferred by the Committee |

Full Members shall be entitled to use all Club facilities and to introduce guests on payment of the appropriate green fee. Junior Members shall be entitled to use the courts at such times as the Committee shall determine and shall not be eligible for election to the Committee.

Riverside Racquets Club – Facility Maintenance Manuals

Section 1: Clubhouse Boiler System

1.1 Introduction
This section covers the gas-fired boiler serving the clubhouse heating and hot water. The boiler is located in the plant room off the rear corridor, adjacent to the kit store. Access is via the external door only; the internal door is kept locked and the key is held by the Facilities Manager.

1.2 Model and Technical Data
Manufacturer: Halstead Eden
Model: Eden Combi 32
Gas type: Natural Gas (G20)
Input (net): 28.4 kW
Output (net): 26.0 kW
Flue type: Concentric, horizontal, 60/100 mm
Expansion vessel: 8 litres, pre-charge 1.0 bar
Maximum heating flow temperature: 82°C
DHW flow rate: 12.5 l/min at 35°C rise
Electrical supply: 230 V, 50 Hz, 3 A fused
IP rating: IPX4
CE marking: Yes

1.3 Installation
The Clubhouse Boiler System installation_year is 2010 in the maintenance manual. Record status: current. The installation was carried out by Thameside Heating Services Ltd under contract to the club, with the commissioning certificate dated 15 March 2010. The boiler replaced the previous floor-standing unit which had been in service since the clubhouse extension in 1987. All gas supply and flue work conformed to the then-current Building Regulations and Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations. The installer registered the work with the local authority building control; the completion certificate is filed in the club office, drawer marked "Boiler – Historical".

Note: The original commissioning paperwork was re-issued in 2012 after a water leak in the office filing cabinet. The re-issued certificate carries the same date and reference number (THS-2010-0315) as the original. The club retains the damaged original in a plastic sleeve for reference.

1.4 Operating Instructions

1.4.1 Normal Operation
The boiler is fully automatic and requires no routine user intervention. The room thermostat in the main hall is the primary heating control. Set the desired temperature using the dial on the wall unit (located near the bar hatch). The hot water is pre-set to 60°C and should not be adjusted without consulting the Facilities Manager.

To switch the system on at the start of the season:
1. Check the pressure gauge on the front panel reads between 1.0 and 1.5 bar when cold. If below 1.0 bar, top up using the filling loop beneath the boiler (see 1.6.2).
2. Ensure the gas isolation valve (yellow handle) is in the open position – handle in line with the pipe.
3. Turn the mains switch on the wall next to the boiler to the "ON" position.
4. Press the reset button on the boiler control panel if the display shows a fault code. The display will show a flame symbol when operating normally.
5. Check that the external flue terminal is clear of obstructions (e.g., leaves, bird nests) before first firing.

To switch off at the end of the season:
1. Turn the mains switch to "OFF".
2. Close the gas isolation valve (handle at right angles to the pipe).
3. Do not drain the system unless frost is expected – the boiler has a built-in frost thermostat that operates down to 5°C. If the plant room is unheated and the clubhouse is to be closed for more than two weeks during winter, drain the system following the procedure in 1.6.3.

1.4.2 Seasonal Shutdown Note (from 2024)
Following the December 2023 frost damage to the condensate pipe (see Exception Log, 28/12/23), the Facilities Manager has instructed that the boiler be left in "frost mode" rather than fully shut down during mid-season closures. This means leaving the mains switch on and the gas valve open, with the room thermostat set to 10°C. The boiler will fire briefly to protect the pipework. This applies to closures of up to 10 days. For longer closures, follow the full shutdown procedure above.

| Task | Frequency | Notes |
|------|-----------|-------|
| Brush courts | Weekly (Apr–Sep), fortnightly (Oct–Mar) | Use the drag brush in the direction of play. Do not use a power brush on the surface. |
| Sweep line markings | Weekly | Use a soft broom. Do not use a metal scraper. |
| Check infill levels | Monthly | Top up if the pile is visible in more than 10% of the playing area. Use CourtPro silica sand, grade 0.5–1.0mm, mixed with brick dust at a 3:1 ratio. |
| Water courts | As required | Artificial clay does not need watering for play, but light watering in dry spells helps settle dust and reduces surface migration. Do not over-water – standing water can damage the textile backing. |
| Inspect for wear | Quarterly | Pay particular attention to the service boxes and the baseline areas. |
| Clear debris | Weekly | Leaves and litter should be removed promptly. Do not use a leaf blower on the surface – it displaces the infill. |
| Check court surrounds | Monthly | Ensure the perimeter edging is secure and that the rubber crumb walk-off mats are in place at court entrances. |

2.3 Seasonal Preparation

2.3.1 Spring Opening (April)

1. Remove the winter cover (if fitted) and allow the surface to dry fully.
2. Brush the entire surface to redistribute the infill.
3. Check and repair any line markings. The club uses CourtPro acrylic line paint, applied with a 100mm masking tape guide. Allow 24 hours drying time before play.
4. Inspect the floodlighting (see Section 4) and replace any failed lamps.
5. Check the nets and posts. The posts should be wound down fully for the winter and re-set to the correct tension (see Section 2.5).

2.3.2 Autumn Close (October)

1. Give the surface a final brush and sweep.
2. Top up infill levels if required.
3. Remove any debris from the court drains.
4. Fit the winter cover if the club decides to use it. The cover is only recommended if the courts are to be unused for more than six weeks. If the cover is fitted, it must be secured at all edges and checked weekly for wind damage.

2.4 Repairs

2.4.1 Small Tears or Cuts

Small tears (up to 100mm) can be repaired in-house:

1. Clean the area with a soft brush.
2. Apply CourtPro repair adhesive (available from the Facilities Office) to the underside of the torn flap.
3. Press down firmly and weight with a sandbag for 24 hours.
4. Once dry, brush the area to redistribute the infill.

The Courts Surface surface_type is artificial clay. Record status: current.

2.4.2 Larger Damage

For damage larger than 100mm, or if the textile backing is damaged, contact CourtPro directly (telephone number on the inside cover of this manual). Do not attempt to patch large areas in-house – the surface will not play evenly.

2.4.3 Infill Migration

Infill migration is normal, especially at the ends of courts and along the net line. The surface should be brushed regularly to redistribute the infill. If migration is severe (more than 5mm depth loss in any area), top up as described in 2.2.

2.5 Nets and Posts

The nets and posts are the standard club type, supplied by NetPro Ltd (model NP-3). The posts are set in permanent sockets at the side of the court.

- Net height at the centre: 0.914m
- Net height at the posts: 1.07m
- The net should be tensioned so that the centre strap is pulled down to the correct height. The strap is adjusted by turning the ratchet on the post.

The posts should be wound down at the end of the season to reduce wind damage. To wind down:

1. Remove the net from the posts.
2. Turn the handle on top of the post anticlockwise until the post is fully lowered.
3. Cover the socket with the rubber cap provided.

| Defects inspection | Passed, 20/05/2022 (no snags) |
| Warranty | 5 years (workmanship), 10 years (textile from date of installation) |

No further full resurfacing is planned before 2032 at the earliest, subject to the condition
surveys described in section 3.3 below.

3.2 Post-Resurfacing Notes

The first three months after resurfacing (May–July 2022) required extra attention to brushing.
The new textile sheds some loose fibre initially; this is normal and not a defect. The club’s
grounds staff carried out a daily light brush for the first six weeks, then reverted to the
standard weekly schedule set out in section 2.2 of this manual.

A note from the CourtPro site supervisor (handwritten, in the project file): “Surface will play
slightly fast for the first season. Do not top up infill before October 2022 – let it settle
first.” This advice was followed; no infill was added until the autumn close.

3.3 Surface Condition Surveys

The Facilities Manager (or appointed deputy) should carry out a visual condition survey twice
per year, once in spring (after the winter cover is removed) and once in autumn (before the
cover is fitted). The survey is a walk-around inspection, noting any areas of concern on the
form in Appendix B of this manual.

The survey should check:

- Surface wear, especially at the baseline and service line areas
- Infill depth (use the depth gauge in the Facilities Office)
- Any lifting at seams or edges
- Drainage after heavy rain (puddling indicates a base problem)
- Condition of the line markings
- Any damage to the surrounding fence or gate

A copy of each completed survey form should be filed in the Facilities Office and a summary
sent to the Club Committee at the next meeting. If any survey identifies damage greater than
the small-tear category (section 2.4.1), contact CourtPro before carrying out any remedial
work.

3.4 Ongoing Surface Care Guidelines

The following guidelines apply to the current surface (installed 2022) and should be read
alongside the routine maintenance schedule in section 2.2.

1. Brushing. The surface should be brushed once per week during the playing season (April to
   September). Use the club’s CourtPro branded drag brush, available from the store. Brush in
   one direction only, alternating the direction each week. Do not use a stiff-bristle broom –
   this will damage the textile.

**4.3 Routine Servicing**

The boiler must be serviced annually, ideally in the late summer (August or September)
before the heating season begins. The club’s service contract is with Thameside Heating
Services (contact: 020 7946 0821, ask for the commercial desk). The current contract runs
to 31 December 2025 and includes one service visit per year plus call-out at a reduced
rate.

The service must include, as a minimum:

- Check of flue termination and flue seals
- Check of condensate trap and drain line (blockage is a common fault)
- Combustion analysis with a calibrated analyser (record readings on the service sheet)
- Check of expansion vessel pre-charge pressure
- Check of the pressure relief valve (lift the lever briefly to confirm free movement)
- Check of the magnetic filter (clean if required)
- Visual check of the gas pipework and the meter connection

A copy of each service report is to be filed in the Facilities Office and the log book
updated. The Facilities Manager should be notified if any part fails or is found to be
at risk.

**4.5 Boiler Operation – Normal Use**

The boiler is controlled by a simple programmable timer in the plant room (Honeywell
ST9420). The timer is set as follows:

- Weekdays: 06:00 – 09:00 and 16:00 – 22:00
- Weekends: 07:00 – 22:00

The timer should be adjusted only by the Facilities Manager. During the summer months
(June to August inclusive) the heating side of the boiler is switched off at the isolator;
hot water remains available via the immersion heater in the cylinder. The immersion
heater is on a separate time switch, set for 05:00 – 07:00 daily.

To switch the heating back on for the autumn, the Facilities Manager should:

1. Switch on the isolator (green lever, plant room wall).
2. Check the system pressure gauge reads between 1.0 and 1.5 bar. If below 1.0 bar,
   top up via the filling loop (silver braided hose, left of the boiler) until the gauge
   reads 1.2 bar, then close both valves fully.
3. Check the timer is set to the winter schedule.
4. Turn the boiler thermostat to 60 °C for the first 24 hours, then to the normal
   setting of 70 °C.

**5. CLUBHOUSE ROOF**

**5.1 General**

The clubhouse roof is a pitched design with interlocking concrete tiles over a
breathable membrane. The roof covers the main hall, changing rooms, and the
upper-floor viewing gallery. Access to the roof is by ladder via the hatch in the
store room ceiling (key held in the Facilities Office). Only authorised contractors
or Facilities staff may go onto the roof. Two persons should be present whenever
the hatch is used.

**5.2 Inspection Schedule**

| Interval | Item | Action |
|---|---|---|
| After any storm (wind over 45 mph) | Tiles, ridge, valleys | Visual check from ground and, if safe, from the hatch. Note any slipped or missing tiles. |
| April and October | Valleys and gutters | Clear leaves and debris. Check lead flashing at the chimney and abutment walls. |
| Annually (spring) | Whole roof | Full inspection from a ladder or via the hatch. Check tile condition, mortar bedding at the ridge, and the condition of the membrane at the eaves. |
| Every 5 years | Roof structure | Check timber trusses for damp, insect attack, or deflection. Report any findings to the Facilities Manager. |

The roof was re-felted and re-tiled in 2016 (works by J. Bradshaw & Son,
Roofing Contractors). The original timber structure is retained. No major
defects have been recorded since the re-tiling. Minor maintenance only has been
required.

**5.3 Known Issues and Local Notes**

- The valley gutter above the main hall entrance can hold water after heavy rain
  if the outlet is blocked. Check the outlet grid before the winter months.
- A small number of tiles on the north-facing slope have a slight moss growth.
  This is cosmetic and does not affect the weathertightness. The moss should not
  be treated with a pressure washer as this can damage the tile surface.
- The lead flashing around the chimney was replaced in 2021 after a leak was
  reported. The leak was traced to a split in the old flashing, not to the tiles.
- The roof hatch hinges should be oiled twice a year (spring and autumn). Use a
  light oil, not grease, to avoid attracting dust.

**5.4 Repair Procedure – Slipped or Missing Tiles**

If a tile is found to be slipped or missing, do not attempt to repair it from
inside the roof space. The repair should be carried out from the roof surface by
a competent person. The procedure is as follows:

1.  Remove the two tiles above the damaged tile to gain access.
2.  Lift the damaged tile out, taking care not to damage the membrane beneath.
3.  Slide the new tile into position, engaging the nibs on the batten.
4.  Replace the two upper tiles.
5.  Do not use mortar or sealant to fix the tile; the tile should be held by the
    battens and its own nibs. If the batten is damaged, stop and report to the
    Facilities Manager.

Spare tiles are stored in the plant room, on the shelf above the boiler. There
are approximately 20 tiles in stock. The tiles are Marley Modern, colour
"Brown".

**5.5 Flat Roof Sections**

There are two flat roof sections over the ground-floor store rooms (either side
of the main entrance). These are felt roofs with a mineral surface. They were
last overlaid in 2019. The felt is in fair condition. Blisters have appeared in a
couple of places but have not split. Do not walk on these roofs unless absolutely
necessary. If access is required, use a crawling board to spread the load.

Inspect the flat roofs at the same time as the main roof (April and October).

**6. ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS**

**6.1 General**

The electrical installation at the club is a three-phase supply, incoming at
the meter cupboard on the north wall of the plant room. The distribution board
is labelled DB1 and is located in the plant room, to the left of the boiler.
All circuits are identified on the schedule fixed to the inside of the board
door. A second board, DB2, serves the clubhouse first floor and is located in
the corridor cupboard outside the ladies changing room.

Isolation points: the main switch for DB1 is at the meter cupboard. There is
a separate isolator for the floodlights, mounted on the wall outside the
plant room, next to the fire alarm panel. This isolator is switched off at
all times except during floodlight operation.

Any electrical work, including the replacement of lamps, must be carried out
by a qualified electrician. Club staff are not authorised to open any
distribution board or work on live circuits. If a circuit breaker trips
repeatedly, do not reset it more than once. Report the fault to the
Facilities Manager.

**6.2 Floodlight Control Panel**

The floodlight installation consists of six columns around the two main
courts (courts 1 and 2). Each column carries two fittings. The control panel
is a Timeguard TGLP360, located in the plant room on the wall above the
workbench. It provides automatic dusk-to-dawn switching with a manual
override.

The panel was installed in March 2015. The original photocell was replaced in
2019 after intermittent switching was reported. The current photocell is a
Timeguard TLG90.

Operating notes:

- The automatic mode is selected by pressing the AUTO button. The MANUAL
  mode should only be used for testing or when the photocell has failed.
- The override switch is labelled "ON" and "OFF". Do not leave the override
  in the ON position. The floodlights should not be left on during daylight
  hours.
- The panel has a test button. Pressing this simulates darkness and should
  bring the lights on within a few seconds. Use the test button only during
  daylight.

Maintenance schedule (floodlights):

| Task | Frequency | Notes |
|------|-----------|-------|
| Clean photocell lens | Monthly | Wipe with a dry cloth. Do not use solvents. |
| Check fittings for water ingress | Quarterly | Look for condensation inside the lens. |
| Check column fixings and guy wires | Annually (April) | Tighten if loose. |
| Lamp replacement | As required | Use 400W metal halide lamps. |
| Test panel operation | Annually (October) | Use the test button, record in log. |

The lamp in the fitting nearest the gate (column 3) has been replaced more
often than the others. This is thought to be due to vibration from the gate
closing. If this lamp fails again, consider fitting a different lamp type.

**6.3 Fire Alarm System**

The fire alarm is a conventional two-wire system, with a control panel
manufactured by Kentec Electronics (model Syncro AS). The panel is located in
the corridor outside the plant room, adjacent to the main entrance to the
courts. There are manual call points at the following locations:

- Main entrance, inside the door
- Corridor outside the plant room
- Top of the stairs to the first floor
- Kitchen, by the service hatch

There are no automatic smoke or heat detectors in the original installation.
The system relies on manual call points only. A review in 2022 recommended
the addition of smoke detectors in the kitchen and the first-floor corridor,
but this work has not yet been carried out. See section 6.6 for the current
status of this recommendation.
